ioSurfaces.name: Default.aspx - Fleet status board
ioSurfaces.description: Main fleet grid. On every load it reads the session FltIdentity (or redirects to Login), then binds FleetGridView from AircraftStatusManager.GetList(ProgId=0, ..., ShowOffTest=False), which calls the stored procedure listAircraftStatuses. It shows location, MSN (FRC #), status (UP is green, DOWN is red), the hangar and Contoso comments, and the last update in PT. The grid sorts by Location, MSN or Date through a hidden field. Clicking a status redirects to EditAircraftStatus.aspx?v=<AircraftId>. OFF TEST aircraft are filtered out in code.

ioSurfaces.name: OffTestFleet.aspx - Fleet board including OFF TEST aircraft
ioSurfaces.description: Same grid as Default.aspx, but GetList is called with ShowOffTest=True, so aircraft whose status is OFF TEST are also listed. It reads from listAircraftStatuses and links to EditAircraftStatus.aspx.

ioSurfaces.name: EditAircraftStatus.aspx - Edit one aircraft's status
ioSurfaces.description: Loads one aircraft via AircraftStatusDB.GetItem (stored procedure fetchAircraftStatus) from the query-string value v. It shows MSN, a status drop-down (OFF TEST, UP, DOWN), the engineer comment and the hangar comment. The controls are disabled unless AircraftStatusManager.CanEdit passes, which needs the Fleet CanEdit permission plus a per-role time window from the appSettings ChangeTime*For<RoleId> keys (superusers are exempt). Save calls AircraftStatusDB.SaveStatusUpdate (stored procedure updateAircraftStatus) and redirects to Default.aspx.

ioSurfaces.name: Login.aspx - User sign-in
ioSurfaces.description: An ASP.NET Login control posts the username and password to FltIdentityManager.AuthenticateUserLogin (in FLTBizObjects). On success it stores the FltIdentity in Session("fltIdentity") and redirects to default.aspx. On failure it shows a failure message and writes the exception through Logger.Write.

ioSurfaces.name: Logout.aspx - Sign-out
ioSurfaces.description: Calls FltIdentityManager.LogOut on the session identity, clears and abandons the session, expires the ASP.NET_SessionId cookie and redirects to Login.aspx.

ioSurfaces.name: password_recovery.aspx - Forgotten password reset
ioSurfaces.description: Takes a username, looks it up with FltUserManager.GetItem and, if the user exists, calls FltUserManager.GenerateNewPassword (in FLTBizObjects, which resets and delivers the new password). It always switches to the confirmation view, whether or not the user was found.

ioSurfaces.description: The console job calls FltExportManager.CreateDownloadFile with the AppSettings DownloadPath folder. It writes a Programs > Program > Fleet > Aircraft > Locations > Usages/WorkOrders XML hierarchy to Temp_Download_*.xml and then renames it to Download_*.xml. The console App.config has no 'appPrefix' key, so the prefix in the file name is empty.

ioSurfaces.name: Export XML writer (FltExportManager.BuildDownloadFile)
ioSurfaces.description: Creates the temporary XML file in the download folder with XmlTextWriter, writes every program, and renames the temp file to its final name once it is complete.

ioSurfaces.name: Console output

ioSurfaces.name: Form1 (WinForms main window)
ioSurfaces.description: The only screen in this desktop tool. It is the startup form (Application.myapp MainForm=Form1) and has one control, Button1 (caption 'Button1'). Clicking the button starts the download. There are no input fields, so the user cannot enter credentials, a URL or a target path.

ioSurfaces.name: POST to FLT download service (test.download.flt.contoso.example)
ioSurfaces.description: Button1_Click sends an HTTP POST to the hardcoded URL https://test.download.flt.contoso.example. The body is an XML <request> holding a hardcoded loginName 'devuser', a password (redacted in the source) and action 'getFile'. The Content-Type is application/x-www-form-urlencoded even though the body is XML, and the request also sends the Windows default credentials (CredentialCache.DefaultCredentials). The URL points at a test host, and the credentials are in the source code.

ioSurfaces.name: Downloaded FLT file written to local disk
ioSurfaces.description: The response stream is copied in 4096-char chunks into a FileStream opened with FileMode.OpenOrCreate at strLocalPath. strLocalPath is declared at line 10 but never assigned anywhere in the module, so the FileStream constructor gets Nothing and would throw ArgumentNullException at runtime. Two more defects: OpenOrCreate does not truncate an existing file, and writer.Write always writes the full buffer size, not the number of chars Read returned, so the last chunk can leave stale or padded data.
